Ukrainian Navy spokesperson Captain 2nd Rank Dmytro Pletenchuk said the bridge’s functionality could be reduced to the point where people traveling between Crimea and Taman would have to cross railway tracks on foot, carrying backpacks. He added that the alternative land route through Russian-occupied southern Ukraine remains under Ukrainian fire control, describing it as a road of fury and death. The Kerch Bridge and the occupied southern land corridor are two critical connections between Russia and Crimea. Severely restricting the bridge while maintaining fire control over the alternative route would complicate Russian military logistics, particularly the movement of equipment, ammunition, and reinforcements. Pletenchuk’s remarks signal Ukraine’s intention to keep both supply routes under pressure. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet
